reconstructed_theorem_text: For every natural number n ≥ 2 and every a ∈ ℝⁿ with ‖a‖ = 1, where ℝⁿ has its standard Euclidean inner product and norm, define H_a: ℝⁿ → ℝ by H_a(x) = (1 − ‖x‖²)/‖x − a‖ⁿ, using ordinary real division and the natural-number power n in the denominator. Then H_a is harmonic on a neighborhood of each point of ℝⁿ ∖ {a}: for every x ≠ a it is twice continuously real-differentiable at x, in the local sense of the approved C² context, and its actual Euclidean Laplacian is identically zero on some neighborhood of x. The Laplacian is the orthonormal trace of the actual second Fréchet derivative. This conclusion covers every point other than a, including points inside, on, and outside the unit sphere whenever they differ from a; no conclusion is asserted at a.
